summary: In Greek mythology, Antiphus or Antiphos (Ancient Greek Ἄντιφος) is a name attributed to many men. The atlas node antiphus-thessalus-cos is the Coan captain — son of Thessalus son of Heracles and brother of Pheidippus — who with his brother leads the island contingent (Cos, Calydnae, Carpathus, Casus, Nisyrus) to Troy with thirty ships, and in later tradition gives Thessaly its name from their father.

sections.heading: Coan captain at Troy
paragraphs: Homer's Catalogue of Ships pairs Antiphus and Pheidippus as sons of Thessalus leading the Coans and their island dependencies. Apollodorus and Hyginus preserve the same double command; a later belief makes Antiphus the invader who names a region of Greece Thessaly after his father.

Homonym guard: not Antiphus son of Priam; not the Maeonian ally Antiphus son of Talaemenes (antiphus-maeonian); not Odysseus' companion eaten by Polyphemus; not the Phthian son of Myrmidon. The atlas id is the Coan Heraclid captain alone.
